visual.general_description: Line chart of serum sodium over hospital days with rows of medication dose markers and a legend.
visual.detailed_description: Line chart with markers on a white background: a blue line with round blue markers (legend "Serum Na+") plots serum sodium against time in days in the lower part of the plot. The x-axis is titled "Time (days)" with printed ticks 0 to 13 in steps of one; the y-axis is titled "Serum sodium (meq/dl)" with printed ticks 100, 110, 120, 130 and 140. No data labels are printed on the line. Qualitatively the sodium line starts high at the left, falls over the first days, rises briefly, then falls to a trough in the middle of the plot, rises to a peak after that, falls again, and ends with a rise at the right edge. Above the sodium line, separate rows of symbols mark medication dose timings along the x-axis, with a legend at the right listing: Amiodarone 400 mg PO (orange diamonds), Amiodarone 200 mg PO (open orange diamonds), Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg (blue circles), Furosemide 40 mg IV (yellow circles), Lisinopril 20 mg (green squares), Tolvaptan 15 mg (dark blue triangles), Tolvaptan 30 mg (black triangle), Desmopressin 2 µg IV (purple circles) and NaCl 1 g PO (brown triangles). Amiodarone 400 mg symbols cluster at the left of the plot and the 200 mg symbols follow them; the tolvaptan, desmopressin and NaCl symbols appear in later rows further right, and the lisinopril squares are spread across the plot.

clinical_significance.statement: The article states that the figure depicts the patient's serum sodium levels and the administration times of medications that can alter sodium.

evidence.quote: The serum Na levels and administration times of potentially Na level-altering medications are depicted in Figure 1.

limitations: The legend prints a lisinopril 20 mg entry, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg and NaCl 1 g PO, which the article text does not state (the text gives NaCl 3 g/day and no lisinopril); legend text is recorded as printed and no clinical fact is derived from it.
The sodium axis is printed in meq/dl whereas the text uses meq/l; kept as printed.
Overlapping markers in the dose rows could not be counted reliably, so no dose counts or times are recorded.
